project.objective: Before his marriage to Clara Amelia Palacios Oliva, did Ciriaco Bardales have a son by a Carmen Morales — an infant Ciriaco who died 12 August 1905 in Guatemala City?

questions.question: Was the infant Ciriaco who died 12 August 1905 in Guatemala City the son of Ciriaco Bardales and Carmen Morales, conceived before his marriage to Clara Amelia Palacios Oliva?
questions.rationale: The user's objective is a single-fact question about the parentage of a specific infant. Guatemala City maintained civil registration of deaths from 1877 onward; the 1905 death register is the primary record most likely to name both parents. This question maps directly to the objective and is testable against civil registration records held in Guatemala.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: All three sources (src_001 infant death 12 Aug 1905, src_002 sibling José Luis death 4 Oct 1954, src_003 infant birth 1 Aug 1905) have had their original register images examined and confirmed by image-reader agents (log_009, log_010, log_011). The prior blocking criteria — original_substitution and evidence_class — are now met. Original image log_011 resolved the 'Bandales/Bardales' transcription ambiguity: the handwritten register shows 'Bardales' three times (margin index, entry body, and father's own signature), eliminating the only tentative value. Both sub-parts of the question are answered: (A) infant Ciriaco is confirmed son of Ciriaco Bardales and Carmen Morales by three original civil registrations with different informants; (B) the relationship predates any marriage to Clara Amelia Palacios Oliva, documented across FAN evidence spanning 1896–1905 — a 9-year pre-marital relationship confirmed by multiple corroborating registrations. No competing evidence exists. Overturn risk is low.

stop_criteria.goal_alignment: MET. Both sub-parts answered. (A) Three original civil registrations confirm infant Ciriaco as son of Ciriaco Bardales and Carmen Morales: his own civil birth registration 1 Aug 1905 (src_003, original image log_011 — father personally signed 'Bardales' three times), his civil death registration 12 Aug 1905 (src_001, original image log_009 — parents named as solteros from Chiquimula), and sibling José Luis Bardales Morales's civil death registration 4 Oct 1954 (src_002, original image log_010 — same parents named 49 years later). (B) The Bardales–Palacios Oliva civil marriage was not found despite three search approaches (log_004, log_005, log_006); FAN evidence (log_008) documents the Bardales–Morales relationship from at least 1896, a full 9 years before the infant's death; Clara Amelia Palacios was born 1885, making a marriage before 1896 implausible. The 'before his marriage' premise is established inferentially with high confidence. proof-conclusion should state the appropriate tier honestly.
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: MET. Searched: FamilySearch collection 2075150 (Guatemala City civil registration deaths 1905 — pli_001, positive), civil births 1903–1905 (pli_002, positive), marriage records via three approaches groom+bride sides 1890–1920 (pli_004, negative across 262 results examined); FamilySearch collection 1614809 (Catholic church records 1903–1906 — pli_003, negative); FAN search for Carmen Morales + Ciriaco Bardales 1895–1920 (pli_005, positive, 4+ children spanning 1896–1905+). Original images examined for all three found records (log_009, log_010, log_011). Fallback repositories (Ancestry 9884, browse-only indexes, full-text co-occurrence) appropriately skipped as the primary records were located. Name variants covered (Bardalez, Vardalez, and the encountered 'Bandales' in the index). No additional relevant jurisdiction identified. Guatemala City civil registration began 1877 (FamilySearch Wiki, Guatemala Civil Registration), well before the 1905 events.
stop_criteria.original_substitution: MET. All three derivative index entries have been superseded by examination of the original handwritten register images. src_001 (infant death): original image ark:/61903/3:1:939J-5HZ1-J examined in log_009, Partida 680 confirmed. src_002 (José Luis death): original image ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS7W-CHN1 examined in log_010, Acta 3640 confirmed. src_003 (infant birth): original image ark:/61903/3:1:939J-CQ9P-F7 examined in log_011, Partida 1118 confirmed — the index transcription 'Bandales' was confirmed as a misread of the handwritten 'Bardales'. GPS standard is satisfied.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: MET. Three genuinely independent civil registration events with different informants: (1) infant Ciriaco's civil birth registration 1 Aug 1905 (src_003) — father Ciriaco Bardales personally appeared and signed; (2) infant Ciriaco's civil death registration 12 Aug 1905 (src_001) — different registration event, different registrar; (3) sibling José Luis Bardales Morales's civil death registration 4 Oct 1954 (src_002) — a different child, 49 years later, different informant (likely surviving spouse Marta Castro). Three independent informants, three independent creation events. FAN records (log_008) further corroborate the parental couple across multiple children 1896–1905+. Two separate informant streams constitute well over the minimum threshold.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: MET. The civil birth registration src_003 (original image confirmed, log_011) is an original record with primary information: the father Ciriaco Bardales personally appeared before the civil registrar, declared the child his natural son of Carmen Morales, and signed his own name — all documented in the original handwritten register. The civil death registration src_001 (original image confirmed, log_009) is an original record; the death date/place information is primary (registrar's official duty). Both are now accessed in original form, not derivative.
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: MET. No formal conflicts are registered (conflicts section: 0 items). The sole prior discrepancy — the index reading 'Bandales' vs. 'Bardales' in src_003 — has been resolved by original image examination (log_011): the handwritten register shows 'Bardales' three times, confirming the index was a transcription error. The tentative marker on assertion a_031 should be cleared by record-extraction. No records name a different father or mother for the infant. No record establishes the Bardales–Palacios Oliva marriage as pre-dating the infant's 1905 birth.
stop_criteria.overturn_risk: LOW — MET. Three original civil registrations are concordant and confirmed from original images. The father personally signed the birth register. FAN evidence documents the Bardales–Morales parental relationship across at least four children spanning 1896–1905. No unsearched record type is likely to name different parents for this infant: baptism records searched (negative for indexed entries); marriage records searched (Bardales–Morales union not found and both described as solteros, consistent with a non-marital relationship). The one theoretical risk — finding a Bardales–Palacios Oliva marriage certificate predating 1896 — is implausible given Clara Amelia's 1885 birth year (she would have been at most 11 in 1896) and is contradicted by FAN evidence. The absence of the civil marriage record between Ciriaco Bardales and Clara Amelia Palacios Oliva is noted: it was not located in civil records despite three search approaches, but children's records (log_004) and Clara Amelia's death record confirm the marriage did occur. Its exact date remains unverified in civil records; proof-conclusion should note this limitation and calibrate the tier accordingly.

items.rationale: The civil death registration for the infant Ciriaco, who allegedly died 12 August 1905 in Guatemala City, is the primary target. Collection 2075150 ('Guatemala, Guatemala, Civil Registration, 1874–2008') is the department-level indexed collection covering Guatemala City deaths; it carries 4.2M indexed records. Per loc_001, death records in this series record the date and place of death, the name and age of the deceased, and — critically — the names of both parents. A matching entry naming Ciriaco Bardales as father and Carmen Morales as mother would be direct evidence answering q_001. Search on the infant's given name 'Ciriaco' with surname 'Bardales' and death year 1905 in Guatemala. Also try 'Bardales' without a given name to catch indexing variants. Variant surname spellings to try: Bardalez, Vardalez.

If the infant died in August 1905 as an infant, a civil birth registration for him likely exists in Guatemala City civil records from late 1904 or early 1905 (possibly also 1903 if 'infant' is broadly defined). Collection 2075150 covers births as well as deaths; birth records in this series name both parents directly. Finding the birth record corroborates the parentage stated in the death record and provides a second civil registration event. Search on given name 'Ciriaco', surname 'Bardales', birth years 1903–1905 in Guatemala City. Per loc_001 quirk, the same indexed collection covers births and deaths.

Catholic parish records for Guatemala City are a parallel source to civil registration. Collection 1614809 ('Guatemala, Catholic Church Records, 1581–2023') is indexed at FamilySearch with 5M+ records and covers baptisms, marriages, and burials. The FamilySearch Catalog item 'Registros parroquiales, 1897–1930' (catalog 287533) covers our period in browse-only images. An infant baptism entry naming Ciriaco Bardales and Carmen Morales as parents, or a burial entry for the infant, would corroborate civil registration evidence. Search collection 1614809 for 'Ciriaco Bardales' or 'Ciriaco Morales' in the 1903–1906 window. If indexed search fails, browse catalog 287533.

The question asks whether the infant predates Ciriaco Bardales's marriage to Clara Amelia Palacios Oliva. A civil marriage record for Ciriaco Bardales and Clara Amelia Palacios Oliva in Guatemala City would establish the date of that marriage, confirming the 'before his marriage' premise and showing whether the infant Ciriaco's August 1905 death preceded it. Both persons are in the tree (KNYF-2Z8 and L6PW-W6G) without sourced marriage dates. Search collection 2075150 for a marriage entry naming Ciriaco Bardales and Clara (or Amelia) Palacios in Guatemala, 1900–1920. Per the record-type guide, the parents' marriage record also: (a) confirms the couple as a unit; (b) by its date relative to the 1905 infant death, corroborates or refutes whether Carmen Morales was a prior relationship. Note: this item targets the Bardales–Palacios Oliva marriage, not the alleged Bardales–Morales union.

Mandatory FAN item for this parentage question. Carmen Morales is the alleged mother of the infant; any civil registration record in Guatemala City naming her — a marriage to Ciriaco Bardales, a marriage to someone else (which would help date her relationships), her own death record naming her parents, or a birth record for another child — would corroborate her identity and her relationship to Ciriaco Bardales. Search collection 2075150 for 'Carmen Morales' in Guatemala, 1895–1920, to surface any records where she appears as a principal. Lifespan window for Carmen Morales set at 1895–1920, which accommodates her being a young adult at the 1905 birth/death.

Fallback if FamilySearch search (pli_001) yields no death record for the infant. Ancestry holds 'Guatemala, Civil Registration, 1877–1980' (collection 9884), indexed + images, which covers the same Guatemala City 1905 death records from a different indexing effort. Different indexers may have transcribed the infant's name or parents' names differently, so a separate search here could surface a record the FamilySearch index missed. Search for 'Ciriaco Bardales' death in Guatemala, 1905. Also try 'Ciriaco Morales' (infant might be indexed under mother's surname).

Full-text co-occurrence search for 'Bardales' AND 'Morales' as co-occurring surnames within the Guatemala civil registration corpus, routed to the search-full-text skill. Per the record-type guide, a full-text co-occurrence search across unscoped AI-transcribed page text can surface records where name-indexing failed (an infant's name mis-transcribed, a record with an unusual layout). Searching '+Bardales +Morales' unscoped in Guatemala civil records 1900–1910 would surface any document where both surnames appear together — a birth entry, an acknowledgment of paternity, or a death record that the indexed search missed. Execute via search-full-text skill, not record_search.

Fallback if both indexed searches (pli_001 and pli_006) and the full-text search (pli_007) fail. Three browse-only image groups constitute an 'Índice de defunciones, 1900–1910' for Guatemala City (image groups M9CC-KL8, M9CC-KLD, M9CC-KLZ, ~1,271 total images). These are alphabetical name indexes to the death registers, 0% name-searchable and not full-text. Browsing them manually under 'B' for Bardales could locate the infant's entry and point to the specific register volume and entry number before reading the full record image. Routed to search-images skill for page-by-page browsing.

proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Proof Summary: Parentage and Pre-Marital Conception of the Infant Ciriaco Bardales (died 12 August 1905)

**Research Question:** Was the infant Ciriaco who died 12 August 1905 in Guatemala City the son of Ciriaco Bardales and Carmen Morales, conceived before his marriage to Clara Amelia Palacios Oliva?

**Conclusion (conjunctive):** The conjunctive question is answered at **probable** — the strength of its weaker half. Claim A (parentage) is proved; claim B (pre-marital conception) is probable. A conjunctive conclusion rises only to the tier of its weaker component. The scalar `tier` field in the structured record carries `proved` as bookkeeping (the strongest per-claim tier, per schema requirement), but the operative conclusion for the compound question as a whole is probable.

---

### The Evidence

Three original civil registration records from Guatemala City, examined from original handwritten register images, establish the infant's parentage. Guatemala's civil registration system began in 1877; the 1905 records are original government documents.

**1. Civil birth registration, 1 August 1905 (src_003)**

On 1 August 1905, Ciriaco Bardales personally appeared before the civil registrar in Guatemala City and declared that his son Ciriaco had been born that morning at 12:45 a.m. at Casa No. 25, Avenida del Golfo. He stated the child was his natural son (*hijo natural del exponente*) by Carmen Morales, both of them unmarried (*ambos solteros*), ladinos, and natives of Chiquimula la Sierra residing in Guatemala City. He signed his own name — "Ciriaco Bardales" — appearing three times on the page: in the margin index, in the body of the entry, and as his handwritten signature. The original image (ark:/61903/3:1:939J-CQ9P-F7) confirms the surname as "Bardales"; the FamilySearch index transcription "Bandales" is a confirmed misread of the handwritten register. *"Guatemala, Guatemala, Registro Civil, 1874-2008", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:6KNJ-27P8 : accessed 18 September 2026), Entry for Ciriaco Bardales and Ciriaco Bandales, 1 de agosto de 1905.* This is an original record. The father's declaration of the infant's name, parentage, and his own marital status carries primary information quality (self-reporting in person). The child's birth facts carry primary information quality (father as eyewitness). Evidence is direct for parentage and for the father's marital status.

**2. Civil death registration, 13 August 1905 (src_001)**

The day after the child's death — 13 August 1905 — Ciriaco Bardales personally appeared before the civil registrar and reported that "ayer á las tres p. m., en la casa Nº. 25. de la Av. del Golfo, falleció de inflamación y á la edad de doce días, Ciriaco, hijo natural del exponente y de Carmen Morales, solteros, ladinos, católicos, de Chiquimula y de este vecindario." The father did not sign ("no firmó"), but he appeared and ratified the record. The original image (ark:/61903/3:1:939J-5HZ1-J) was examined and confirms all details. *"Guatemala, Guatemala, Registro Civil, 1874-2008", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:6D38-BQ8L : 18 Sep 2026), Entry for Ciriaco Bardales and Ciriaco Bardales, 13 Aug 1905.* This is an original record. The father's self-report of his own marital status ("soltero") carries primary information quality. The death date and place recorded by the civil registrar carry primary information quality (official duty). Evidence is direct for parentage and marital status.

**Source independence note — the two 1905 registrations.** The birth registration (src_003) and the death registration (src_001) are distinct civil acts — different dates, different legal events — but they share the same informant: Ciriaco Bardales himself appeared personally at both. They do not constitute two independent informant streams. What they demonstrate is the father's consistent declarations across two separate legal obligations twelve days apart, each carrying a distinct penalty for false statement. Those declarations are concordant and mutually reinforcing, but they count as one informant's voice, not two independent witnesses.

**3. Civil death registration of José Luis Bardales Morales, 4 October 1954 (src_002)**

Nearly half a century later, the civil death registration of José Luis Bardales Morales — a son of Ciriaco Bardales and Carmen Morales who survived to adulthood — provides the genuinely independent informant stream. The original register image (ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS7W-CHN1) records: "José Luis Bardales Morales de cincuentiseis años, casado con Marta Castro, Litógrafo, hijo de Ciriaco Bardales y Carmen Morales, originario de esta Ciudad." The informant was **Alfredo Chancilla** — not Ciriaco Bardales, not a member of the immediate nuclear family — providing a wholly independent source separated from the 1905 registrations by 49 years. *"Guatemala, Guatemala, Registro Civil, 1874-2008", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:Z9GZ-P9PZ : accessed 18 September 2026), entry for José Luis Bardales Morales; digital image of indexed death registration, Guatemala City, 4 October 1954.* This is an original record. The parentage information is secondary (Alfredo Chancilla was not present at José Luis's birth), but his identification of the same parental couple — for a different child, nearly five decades later — constitutes true independent corroboration. It is this 1954 registration, not the internal agreement of the two 1905 registrations, that supplies the second informant stream necessary to satisfy the GPS independence requirement for the parentage claim.

---

### Analysis and Correlation

**Parentage — claim A (proved).** Two distinct informant streams agree on the parents: (1) the father Ciriaco Bardales's own primary-quality declarations in the 1905 birth and death registrations, and (2) independent informant Alfredo Chancilla in the 1954 death registration of sibling José Luis, naming the same couple for a different child 49 years later. All three registrations were examined from original handwritten images. No competing registration names different parents for the infant. FAN research documents at least four children born to this couple between approximately 1896 and 1905+, establishing a long-standing parental relationship the registrations corroborate. Research is declared exhaustive (pli_001–pli_005, log_001–log_011); all five GPS components are satisfied. Parentage is proved.

**Pre-marital conception — claim B (probable).** Both the birth and death registrations state explicitly that Ciriaco Bardales was "soltero" (unmarried/single) as of 1 August 1905 — his own self-report on personal appearance, carrying primary information quality. This directly establishes that he was not married to anyone, including Clara Amelia Palacios Oliva, when the infant was born. Conception approximately nine months prior — around November 1904 — therefore also preceded any documented marriage to Clara Amelia.

No civil marriage record between Ciriaco Bardales and Clara Amelia Palacios Oliva was located in civil registration records despite three search approaches covering groom-side, bride-side, and combined searches (pli_004, 262 results examined). Children's records and Clara Amelia's death record confirm the marriage occurred, but its exact date remains unverified in searched civil records. The FAN evidence documents the Bardales–Morales relationship from at least 1896 (pli_005, multiple children), and Clara Amelia Palacios Oliva was born 11 June 1886 — making her approximately 10 years old in 1896 and any earlier marriage legally implausible. The overall weight of evidence makes it highly probable that the infant Ciriaco was conceived before Ciriaco Bardales married Clara Amelia Palacios Oliva.

The tier for this claim is probable, not proved, for two compounding reasons: first, the marriage date to Clara Amelia is not established from civil records searched, leaving a documentary gap in the chain; second, the only direct evidence for the "soltero" status comes from the father's two 1905 declarations — both his voice, not independent witnesses. Alfredo Chancilla's 1954 registration does not address the parents' marital status in 1905. The independent corroboration available for claim A therefore does not extend to claim B, reinforcing the probable tier for the pre-marital conception finding.

---

### Discrepancies Addressed

The FamilySearch index for the 1905 birth registration transcribed the father's surname as "Bandales" rather than "Bardales." Examination of the original register image resolves this: the handwritten surname appears as "Bardales" in three distinct locations on the page (margin index, body of the entry, and the father's own signature). The discrepancy is a transcription error in the index, not a discrepancy in the underlying record.

The 1954 death registration for José Luis carries a FamilySearch indexed birth year of 1903, which would imply age 50–51 at death — inconsistent with the stated age of 56 years in the original register image (which yields birth year ~1898). The original image reading is authoritative. This discrepancy is an index error and does not affect the parentage conclusion.

---

### Conclusion

The compound question is answered at **probable** — the tier of its weaker component. Claim A (parentage) is proved: two independent informant streams — the father's primary-quality 1905 declarations and the independent 1954 informant Alfredo Chancilla — agree on the parents, confirmed from original register images, with no competing evidence. Claim B (pre-marital conception) is probable: the father's own self-reports of "soltero" status at both 1905 events are primary-quality and direct, and the circumstantial evidence (FAN documentation from 1896, Clara Amelia's 1886 birth year) strongly supports the inference — but the marriage date to Clara Amelia is not established in civil records, and the sole direct evidence for unmarried status comes from a single informant stream. The conjunctive conclusion, which requires both A and B, rises only to the tier of its weaker half: probable.

# Locality Guide: Guatemala City (Guatemala, Guatemala, Guatemala) — 1877–1920

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formally founded:** January 2, 1776, after the capital was relocated from Antigua Guatemala following the 1773 'Santa Marta' earthquakes.
- **Administrative center:** Guatemala City is itself the capital of Guatemala and of Guatemala Department.
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Guatemala Department, Guatemala.
- **Population during period:** FamilySearch place_population returned no data for this place; current population approximately 2,110,000 per the FamilySearch Wiki (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ciudad_de_Guatemala,_Guatemala,_Guatemala_Genealogy).
- **Economy:** Commercial, governmental, and ecclesiastical center of Guatemala; artisans, merchants, professionals.
- **Religious denominations:** Overwhelmingly Roman Catholic; the Catholic Church was the primary record-keeper before 1877.
- **Key historical events:** Capital relocated from Antigua 1776; Liberal Reform 1871 (Justo Rufino Barrios) secularized institutions and introduced civil registration; civil registration began 1877.

## Boundary changes
- Guatemala City (Ciudad de Guatemala) has been the national capital and seat of Guatemala Department since 1776; boundaries were stable throughout the civil registration era.
- No predecessor jurisdiction holds civil records for this period — civil registration began here in 1877 under the same municipal authority.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** 1877, at the municipal level, nationwide in Guatemala — per https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Guatemala_Civil_Registration.
- **What exists:** Births, marriages, and deaths from 1877 onward. Catalog also lists some civil records beginning in the 1850s–1870s under specific catalog groupings.
- **Primary indexed collection:** *Guatemala, Guatemala, Civil Registration, 1874–2008* (collection 2075150 at FamilySearch) — 4,245,072 indexed records, 27,035,119 persons, index + images. This is the department-level collection covering Guatemala City. **Digitization level: indexed + images.**
- **Country-wide indexed collection:** *Guatemala, Civil Registration, 1833–2009* (collection 1682771 at FamilySearch) — 2,614,040 records. **Digitization level: indexed + images.**
- **Death records content:** Date and place of death, name and age of deceased, civil status, names of parents, spouse's name if married, sometimes place of burial.
- **Browse-only volume series (death):** Several image groups identified via volume_search covering Guatemala City death records in the 1900–1915 period are 0–99% name-indexed (most are ~97–99% searchable via the indexed collections above). Three 'Índice de defunciones, 1900–1910' image groups (M9CC-KL8, M9CC-KLD, M9CC-KLZ, ~1,271 images total) are 0% searchable and NOT full-text — browse-only alphabetical name indexes useful for locating a specific entry before viewing the full register.
- **Specific catalog item for deaths:** *Defunciones, entierros y exhumaciones, 1871–1920* (catalog 220220 at FamilySearch) — images of Guatemala City death registers through 1920. Search collection 2075150 first; use this catalog for browse-access.
- **Ancestry:** *Guatemala, Civil Registration, 1877–1980* at Ancestry — indexed + images ($).
- **MyHeritage:** *Guatemala, Civil Registration, 1877–2008* at MyHeritage — indexed + images ($).
- **Gaps:** No known systematic destruction reported. Some privacy-law redactions in FamilySearch images. Volume search returned 531 total results; only the first page was examined in detail — additional volumes exist.

### Church records
- **Denomination:** Roman Catholic, dominant from colonial era.
- **Record types:** Baptisms, marriages, burials, confirmations.
- **Primary FamilySearch collection:** *Guatemala, Catholic Church Records, 1581–2023* (collection 1614809) — 5,069,282 records, indexed + images.
- **Indexed baptisms through 1917:** *Guatemala, Baptisms, 1730–1917* (collection 1520627 at FamilySearch; also at Ancestry and MyHeritage, subscription).
- **Indexed deaths through 1880:** *Guatemala, Deaths, 1760–1880* (collection 1520636 at FamilySearch; also at Ancestry and MyHeritage) — predates our target period for this question but useful for Ciriaco Bardales's own birth/early life.
- **Browse-only parish volumes (Guatemala City):** Multiple FamilySearch Catalog items, e.g., Registros parroquiales 1631–1920 (cat. 70906), 1636–1937 (cat. 377809), 1641–1934 (cat. 287315), 1647–1977 (cat. 338170), 1694–1915 (cat. 20538) — images only, must browse page-by-page in Spanish.
- **Parish burial records for 1905:** *Registros parroquiales, 1897–1930* (catalog 287533) — images only; covers our period.
- **Language:** Spanish (and Latin for some sacramental entries).

### Census records
- **National census:** Guatemala held a census in 1877 for Guatemala City; Ancestry and MyHeritage have it indexed. No national census for our target years (1905) is known to FamilySearch.
- **Historical padrones:** Padrones de Guatemala, Ciudad de Guatemala 1668–1887 (catalog 723220) — browse-only images; predates civil registration era.
- **Access:** 1877 census indexed at Ancestry (collection 9958) and MyHeritage.

### Probate and court records
- **Court documents:** *Documentos civiles, 1895–1905* (catalog 8025 at FamilySearch) — images only, browse-only. Covers the target period and may include guardianship, recognitions of paternity, or civil petitions.
- **Guardianship records:** *Tutelas, 1636–1894* (catalog 340878) — predates our period.
- **Notarial records:** *Protocolos y providencias, 1579–1842* (catalog 23207); also *Protocolos* 1508–1898 (catalog 348888) — predates our period.

### Land records
- The FamilySearch Wiki page Guatemala_Land_and_Property was not separately fetched; land records for this period are primarily held at RENAP and the Archivo General de Centroamérica (AGCA).

### Military records
- No specific military collections for Guatemala City in the 1877–1920 period were returned by the tools. Guatemala's military records for this era are primarily held at the AGCA in Guatemala City.

### Cemetery records
- **Major cemeteries in Guatemala City** (per https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ciudad_de_Guatemala,_Guatemala,_Guatemala_Genealogy):
  - El Cementerio General de la Ciudad de Guatemala (20 Calle 4 Avenida 20-00, Zona 3) — the principal public cemetery, in use from the 19th century.
  - Camposanto Los Cipreses (Zona 5), Cementerio Las Flores (Zona 9), and others.
- **Online coverage:** FindAGrave and BillionGraves were not specifically returned for this place; no FamilySearch-curated cemetery links appeared in the external links results.
- **Physical records:** Burial registers at the cemeteries or RENAP; exhumation records 1903–1916 at FamilySearch Catalog (catalog 64434).

### Newspaper records
- *Diario de Centro América* and other Guatemala City newspapers from the 19th–20th century may contain birth, death, and marriage notices. The PERiodical Source Index (PERSI) at the Allen County Public Library (https://www.genealogycenter.info/persi/) covers some Guatemalan periodicals.
- HathiTrust (https://www.hathitrust.org/) and Internet Archive (https://archive.org/) hold some digitized Guatemalan newspapers.

### Immigration/emigration records
- Guatemala City is inland; passenger arrival records for foreign-born persons are held primarily at Guatemalan national archives. No specific immigration collections for this place/period were returned by the tools.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Key collections for Guatemala City | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | *Guatemala, Guatemala, Civil Registration, 1874–2008* (coll. 2075150); *Guatemala, Civil Registration, 1833–2009* (coll. 1682771); *Guatemala, Catholic Church Records, 1581–2023* (coll. 1614809) | Free |
| FamilySearch Catalog | Multiple browse-only image volumes; Defunciones 1871–1920 (cat. 220220); Registros parroquiales 1897–1930 (cat. 287533) | Free (images) |
| Ancestry | *Guatemala, Civil Registration, 1877–1980* (coll. 9884); 1877 Census (coll. 9958); Baptisms 1730–1917; Deaths 1760–1880 | Subscription |
| MyHeritage | *Guatemala, Civil Registration, 1877–2008* (coll. 30203); Baptisms; Deaths | Subscription |

**Coverage of this survey:** volume_search returned 531 total results for Guatemala City, 1895–1915 (Death/Vital/Birth/Religious Death record types); only the first page of results (~50 volumes) was examined in detail. The indexed collections (2075150, 1682771) provide name-searchable access to most 1905 death records and are the recommended first search.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Registro Nacional de las Personas (RENAP), Calzada Roosevelt 13-46, zona 7, Guatemala City, PBX +(502) 24161900, https://www.renap.gob.gt/ | Original civil registration records (births, marriages, deaths) from 1877 onward | In-person or written request (Spanish) |
| Archivo General de Centroamérica (AGCA), Guatemala City | Colonial and 19th-century government records, notarial protocols | In-person |

## Records NOT online
- Sexton registers from El Cementerio General and other private cemeteries are not digitized.
- Military records for the 1877–1920 period are held at the AGCA and not known to be online.
- Some civil registration volumes outside the FamilySearch indexed collections remain in RENAP physical custody and are not yet digitized.

## Known record losses
- No known systematic destruction of Guatemala City civil registration records was reported by the tools or FamilySearch Wiki pages consulted.

## Research tips
- Civil registration of births, marriages, and deaths began in Guatemala in 1877 at the municipal level, when the Civil Registry was separated from the Catholic Church — per https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Guatemala_Civil_Registration. For any event before 1877, use Catholic parish records.
- Search the indexed collection *Guatemala, Guatemala, Civil Registration, 1874–2008* (collection 2075150) first for a 1905 Guatemala City death — this is the primary department-level indexed collection with ~4.2M records.
- If the name index search returns no result, consult the three browse-only 'Índice de defunciones, 1900–1910' image groups (M9CC-KL8, M9CC-KLD, M9CC-KLZ) as an alphabetical finding aid, then access the full death register images.
- Death records in this period are in Spanish and follow a narrative handwritten format; they typically name both parents of the deceased, which is essential for identifying paternity of an infant.
- Guatemala City is the entire research focus — no neighboring-jurisdiction spillover applies, as all 1905 Guatemala City events would have been registered at the Guatemala City civil registry.
- The Getting Started guide advises obtaining the specific town of residence before searching, and notes that city inhabitants may have come from surrounding municipalities — cross-check birth records if the parents' origin is unclear — per https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Guatemala_Getting_Started.
- Some FamilySearch images of Guatemala records have privacy-law redactions that do not typically affect genealogically essential name/date/place fields.
- All records are in Spanish. Use the FamilySearch Spanish Genealogical Word List (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Spanish_Genealogical_Word_List) for vocabulary assistance.
